Analyze this distributed-job recovery incident and deliver an implementable decision table.
Contract: the provider deduplicates requests with the same idempotency key ONLY for 24 hours.
It supports lookup by that key during that period. Different keys may create different effects.
Without a durable provider key/result, local state cannot reveal whether a sent request took effect.
Events: E1 local outbox durably records logical job J, stable key K and payload hash H.
E2 worker W1 records dispatch intent and sends the request. E3 the connection times out;
no acknowledgement/result is committed locally. E4 W1's local lease expires. E5 worker W2
sends the same logical job using the SAME key K. E6 an authenticated lookup within the 24-hour window returns exactly one successful result for K matching H. The provider contract guarantees no second effect for K in this window.
Assess these claims with supported/refuted/unknown, using only the supplied evidence:
C1: two send attempts happened; C2: two external writes definitely happened;
C3: expiry of a local lease proves W1's remote operation did not happen;
C4: changing K to K2 can bypass the provider's same-key deduplication;
C5: a local fencing token alone guarantees exactly-once external effects under this contract.
Design recovery actions for these cases. Return exactly one action per case from
dispatch_new, retry_same_key, reconcile, reuse_result, reject_conflict:
R1: durable evidence proves no dispatch occurred yet, with no competing owner.
R2: a request was sent and timed out; lookup now returns a durable successful result matching the original key and payload.
R3: request sent with unknown result, but provider supports neither deduplication nor lookup.
R4: same logical job already has a durable successful result, but the incoming request has a different payload hash.
R5: a duplicate logical job arrives with a different payload hash.
R6: sent request has unknown result; its old provider deduplication window has expired.
The retry_same_key action means an idempotent resubmission with the ORIGINAL key and payload,
optionally preceded by lookup. reconcile means stop automatic resubmission and establish the
external outcome or seek an explicit resolution; it never means assume failure and repeat.

{"marker":"EVAL_MIGRATION","sql":"-- Atomic, idempotent dedup migration for SQLite 3.45+ (help-desk contacts/tickets).
-- Run on a connection with no active transaction. NOT executed by the authoring agent;
-- delivered for an external evaluator.
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;  -- enforcement stays on for the whole migration; never disabled below

BEGIN IMMEDIATE;

-- Drop first so a stale/incorrect same-name index cannot survive; DDL is transactional.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_contacts_tenant_norm_email;

-- Loser -> winner map, nonmissing identities only (missing rows are never mapped/deleted).
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp.contact_dedup;
CREATE TEMP TABLE contact_dedup (
  loser_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  winner_id INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO temp.contact_dedup (loser_id, winner_id)
SELECT id, winner_id
FROM (
  SELECT
    id,
    FIRST_VALUE(id) OVER (
      PARTITION BY tenant_id, lower(trim(email))
      ORDER BY updated_at ASC, id ASC
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
    ) AS winner_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY tenant_id, lower(trim(email))
      ORDER BY updated_at ASC, id ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM contacts
  WHERE email IS NOT NULL
    AND trim(email) <> ''
)
WHERE rn > 1;

-- Normalize missing emails (empty and all-space) to NULL; each such contact is preserved.
UPDATE contacts
SET email = NULL
WHERE email IS NOT NULL
  AND trim(email) = '';

-- Repoint every ticket off a loser BEFORE deleting losers (FK checks are immediate).
UPDATE tickets
SET contact_id = (
  SELECT d.winner_id
  FROM temp.contact_dedup AS d
  WHERE d.loser_id = tickets.contact_id
)
WHERE contact_id IN (SELECT loser_id FROM temp.contact_dedup);

DELETE FROM contacts
WHERE id IN (SELECT loser_id FROM temp.contact_dedup);

-- Normalize retained nonmissing emails (identity is unchanged by this step).
UPDATE contacts
SET email = lower(trim(email))
WHERE email IS NOT NULL
  AND trim(email) <> ''
  AND email <> lower(trim(email));

-- Constraint created inside the same transaction; also acts as the final validator.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_contacts_tenant_norm_email
ON contacts (tenant_id, lower(trim(email)))
WHERE email IS NOT NULL AND trim(email) <> '';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp.contact_dedup;

Stage work: two independent analyses (data/FK invariants; transaction/retry hazards) ran in parallel, an implementer produced the candidate from both, and a separate reviewer inspected it against concrete counterexamples (window frame and tie-break, missing-row preservation, empty/all-space handling, cross-tenant scoping, repoint-before-delete, ticket id/subject preservation, rollback semantics, second-run idempotence, index expression/predicate parity, no triggers/table rebuild, foreign_keys never disabled). The reviewer returned PASS with no concrete defect; the only change made at delivery is a documented connection setting, PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON, placed before BEGIN (a no-op when already ON, outside the transaction, and it can only enable enforcement, never disable it).

Correctness arguments: (1) Identity is (tenant_id, lower(trim(email))); SQLite trim() removes only U+0020, matching the ordinary-ASCII-space rule, and lower() is the same function used in the dedup partition, the normalization UPDATE and the index, so all three agree. (2) The dedup query is filtered to nonmissing rows (email IS NOT NULL AND trim(email) <> ''), so NULL/''/all-space contacts are never mapped, never deleted, and each survives; they are separately normalized to NULL. (3) Winner = first row of each partition ordered by updated_at ASC, id ASC; the ordering key is unique because id is unique, and the explicit full frame does not change which row is first, so ties on updated_at fall to least id. (5) Winners' id, display_name, tenant_id and updated_at are untouched. (6) The partial unique expression index enforces the rule for future INSERT/UPDATE, is tenant-scoped, and excludes missing emails so they are not made unique. {"marker":"EVAL_MIGRATION","sql":"-- SQLite 3.45+ help-desk contact identity migration.
-- Requires foreign_keys=ON (already set by the caller). No triggers, no table rebuild,
-- no FK disabling. Not executed here; delivered for external evaluation.

BEGIN IMMEDIATE;

-- 1. Drop any prior copy of the migration index so a stale/wrong definition cannot
--    survive a rerun. DDL is transactional and rolls back with everything else.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ux_contacts_tenant_email_norm;

-- 2. Materialize the deterministic loser -> winner mapping once, before any
--    mutation. Identity = tenant_id + lower(trim(email)) for nonmissing emails.
--    Winner = least updated_at, then least id (id is unique, so the order is total).
--    Missing contacts (NULL, '', all ASCII spaces) are excluded entirely, so each
--    is preserved separately and never merged.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp.contact_winner;
CREATE TEMP TABLE contact_winner AS
SELECT c.id AS contact_id,
       (SELECT w.id
          FROM contacts w
         WHERE w.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
           AND w.email IS NOT NULL
           AND trim(w.email) <> ''
           AND lower(trim(w.email)) = lower(trim(c.email))
         ORDER BY w.updated_at, w.id
         LIMIT 1) AS winner_id
  FROM contacts c
 WHERE c.email IS NOT NULL
   AND trim(c.email) <> '';

-- 3. Repoint every ticket that references a loser to that loser's winner.
--    Ticket id and subject are untouched; winner_id is an existing contact id and
--    is never NULL for a loser (each identity group contains at least the loser).
UPDATE tickets
   SET contact_id = (SELECT m.winner_id
                       FROM contact_winner m
                      WHERE m.contact_id = tickets.contact_id)
 WHERE contact_id IN (SELECT m.contact_id
                        FROM contact_winner m
                       WHERE m.contact_id <> m.winner_id);

-- 4. Delete losers only after every ticket has been repointed (FKs stay ON).
DELETE FROM contacts
 WHERE id IN (SELECT m.contact_id
                FROM contact_winner m
               WHERE m.contact_id <> m.winner_id);

-- 5. Normalize retained emails: NULL, '', and all-ASCII-space -> NULL;
--    nonmissing -> lower(trim(email)). Winners keep id, display_name, tenant_id
--    and updated_at; only email is rewritten. No unique index exists at this point,
--    so this cannot collide.
UPDATE contacts
   SET email = NULLIF(lower(trim(email)), '');

-- 6. Enforce the same normalized uniqueness for future INSERT/UPDATE. The partial
--    predicate excludes every missing form, so missing emails stay non-unique;
--    tenant_id is part of the key, so tenants are never merged.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_contacts_tenant_email_norm
    ON contacts (tenant_id, lower(trim(email)))
 WHERE email IS NOT NULL AND trim(email) <> '';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp.contact_winner;

COMMIT;
